title: Student lacks legal basis for data sharing
description: Student may share assignment data without proper legal basis or consent from institution
assumptions: Assumes student is aware of data sharing requirements

title: Student provides excessive personal data
description: Student may include more personal information than necessary for assignment submission
assumptions: Assumes student may include unnecessary metadata

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Assignment data in transit could be intercepted by unauthorized parties
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over network

title: Metadata linking parties
description: Transmission metadata (timestamps, IP addresses) could be used to link student to course
assumptions: Assumes metadata is captured during transmission

title: Unauthorized access to grades portal
description: Grades portal may be accessed by unauthorized personnel or external parties
assumptions: Assumes portal has authentication controls

title: Excessive data retention
description: Portal may retain more student data than necessary for course administration
assumptions: Assumes data retention policies exist

title: Failure to notify about data processing
description: Students may not be notified about how their assignment data is processed and stored
assumptions: Assumes notification mechanisms exist

title: Student identification data shared without proper consent
description: Student ID, course, and requesting role information are shared with the grading service without explicit consent from students, potentially violating data protection principles regarding identification.
assumptions: Assumes students may not have been explicitly informed about this data sharing.

title: Potential lack of lawful basis for data sharing
description: The sharing of student data to the grading service may not have a clear lawful basis under applicable data protection regulations, particularly if not necessary for the stated educational purpose.
assumptions: Assumes the data sharing may not be strictly necessary for grading purposes.

title: Data in transit contains identifying information
description: The data flow itself contains student identifiers (student ID, course, requesting role) that could be intercepted and used to link or identify students during transmission.
assumptions: Assumes data may be transmitted over networks where interception is possible.

title: Risk of unauthorized access to student data
description: The Assignment & Grading Service may store or process student data in a way that increases risk of unauthorized access or disclosure to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes the service may have inadequate access controls.

title: Student data used for identification and profiling
description: The service may use student identifiers to link data across different courses or processes, potentially enabling profiling or tracking of students.
assumptions: Assumes the service may aggregate or link student data across multiple contexts.

title: Unintended consequences of data processing
description: Processing of student data by the grading service may have unintended consequences, such as data being used for purposes other than grading or for purposes students did not expect.
assumptions: Assumes the service may have broader data usage than initially intended.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student Assignment Data
description: The Assignment & Grading Service may share student assignment data (including student ID, course, and submission time) with unauthorized parties or in an insecure manner, leading to potential privacy breaches.

title: Potential Lawfulness Issues in Data Sharing
description: The sharing of student assignment data may not be fully lawful or compliant with applicable privacy regulations, particularly regarding consent and purpose limitation.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Assignment Data
description: The Assignment Store may be accessed by unauthorized individuals, leading to potential disclosure of sensitive student information including submission details.

title: Inadequate Data Retention and Deletion
description: The Assignment Store may retain student assignment data beyond necessary retention periods, failing to properly delete data when no longer needed for legitimate purposes.

title: Data in Transit Privacy Risks
description: Assignment data transmitted from the Grading Service to the Assignment Store may contain metadata or be intercepted during transit, potentially revealing information about students and their submission patterns.

title: Unauthorized data sharing by teacher
description: Teacher may share submission data without proper legal authorization or consent from students, potentially violating privacy laws and data protection regulations.
assumptions: Teacher has access to course submissions but may not have explicit legal authority to share them with the portal system.

title: Unintended disclosure of metadata during transmission
description: Data in transit may contain metadata about the teacher and students that could be used to link or identify parties, potentially revealing sensitive information about course enrollments and student identities.
assumptions: Data transmission may expose metadata such as timestamps, IP addresses, or patterns that could be used for identification.

title: Inadequate data storage security
description: The Grades Portal Web App may not implement adequate security measures for storing teacher-submitted data, potentially leading to unauthorized access or data breaches.
assumptions: The portal system may have insufficient access controls, encryption, or security protocols for storing sensitive educational data.

title: Inaccurate information provided to teacher
description: The portal may not accurately reflect the submission queue or student information, potentially leading to confusion or incorrect assessment of student work.
assumptions: The portal system may have bugs, data synchronization issues, or display errors that affect the accuracy of information presented to the teacher.

title: Lawfulness of data processing
description: The portal may be sharing student submissions with teachers without proper legal basis or consent, potentially violating data protection laws.
assumptions: Assumes the portal operates without explicit legal authorization for this data sharing.

title: Notice of data processing
description: Students may not be adequately informed about what data is being shared with teachers and for what purposes.
assumptions: Assumes students are not provided with clear privacy notices about this specific data flow.

title: Data minimization at source
description: The portal may be sharing more student data than necessary for the intended purpose of displaying submissions to teachers.
assumptions: Assumes the portal shares all submission metadata and content rather than only what is strictly necessary.

title: Data minimization at flow
description: Metadata about the parties (e.g., IP addresses, timestamps, session IDs) in transit could be used to link or identify students and teachers.
assumptions: Assumes data flows include metadata that could be used for re-identification or linking.

title: Unintended disclosure at flow
description: Student submission data could be intercepted during transmission to the teacher.
assumptions: Assumes data may be transmitted over networks without adequate encryption.

title: Accuracy of data at destination
description: The teacher may not verify the accuracy of student submissions before using them for grading or assessment purposes.
assumptions: Assumes the teacher relies on portal-provided data without independent verification.

title: Data minimization at destination
description: The teacher may be storing more student data than necessary for their intended purposes.
assumptions: Assumes the teacher may retain all submission data beyond what is needed for grading.

title: Unintended disclosure at destination
description: The teacher may share student submission data with unauthorized parties (e.g., other teachers, administrators, or third parties).
assumptions: Assumes the teacher may have access to share data beyond authorized recipients.

title: Non-compliance at destination
description: The teacher may not follow privacy regulations when handling student data, such as data retention policies or access controls.
assumptions: Assumes the teacher may not be fully aware of or compliant with applicable privacy laws.

title: Lawful basis for data sharing
description: Teacher may share student data without proper legal basis or consent from the student or parent, potentially violating data protection laws.
assumptions: Assumes teacher has access to student data and may share it without explicit consent.

title: Data minimization at source
description: Teacher may share more data than necessary for the intended purpose, including potentially unnecessary student identifiers or grader information.
assumptions: Assumes teacher may include extraneous data when recording grades.

title: Data interception in transit
description: Student data (grades, feedback, identifiers) transmitted from teacher to portal could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over network without end-to-end encryption.

title: Data linkage through metadata
description: Meta-data about the parties (teacher, student, grader) in the data flow could be used to link or identify individuals, potentially revealing relationships or patterns.
assumptions: Assumes metadata about data flow participants is captured and potentially observable.

title: Unauthorized access to stored data
description: Student data stored in the Grades Portal Web App could be accessed by unauthorized personnel or through security vulnerabilities.
assumptions: Assumes portal has access controls but they may be compromised or insufficient.

title: Inadequate data retention/deletion
description: Student data may not be properly retained or deleted according to policy requirements, leading to unnecessary data retention or inability to comply with data subject rights.
assumptions: Assumes portal has data retention policies but they may not be properly implemented.

title: Excessive Data Collection at Source
description: The grading service may collect and share more data than necessary for the grading purpose, including potentially sensitive student information beyond what is required for grade assignment.
assumptions: Assumes the service collects all fields without justification

title: Inappropriate Information Sharing
description: The grading service may share information that is not appropriate for the intended purpose of grade assignment, potentially including feedback that could be sensitive or inappropriate.
assumptions: Assumes feedback may contain sensitive information

title: Data Integrity During Transmission
description: Grade records may be intercepted or modified during transmission from the grading service to the database, potentially compromising data integrity and student privacy.
assumptions: Assumes data may traverse unsecured networks

title: Data Minimization at Storage
description: The grade records database may store more data than necessary for the intended purpose, potentially including unnecessary metadata or historical records.
assumptions: Assumes database may retain data beyond retention requirements

title: Unintended Consequences of Storage
description: Storing grade records in the database may have unintended consequences, such as enabling profiling or linking of students across courses.
assumptions: Assumes database may be accessed by multiple parties

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Student's grade request data could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission to the grades portal.
assumptions: Assumes standard network transmission without encryption

title: Unauthorized access to grades data
description: The grades portal could disclose student grades to unauthorized parties after receiving the request.
assumptions: Assumes the grades portal has proper access controls

title: Student request interception
description: The student's grade request could be intercepted or misused by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes standard network transmission without encryption

title: Excessive data storage
description: The grades portal might store more student data than necessary for the purpose of providing grades.
assumptions: Assumes the grades portal follows data minimization principles

title: Unlawful data processing
description: The grades portal might process student data in a way that violates privacy laws or regulations.
assumptions: Assumes the grades portal complies with applicable privacy laws

title: Unintended Disclosure of Student Grades
description: The portal may inadvertently disclose student grades to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, misconfiguration, or improper access controls.
assumptions: Assumes the portal has some level of access control but may have gaps.

title: Inaccurate or Outdated Grade Information
description: The portal may display inaccurate, outdated, or incomplete grade information to the student, affecting their ability to make informed decisions about their academic progress.
assumptions: Assumes the portal retrieves data from a central database that may have synchronization issues.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Student grades and teacher feedback transmitted from the portal to the student may be intercepted by unauthorized parties during data transmission, especially if not properly encrypted.
assumptions: Assumes standard web transmission without guaranteed end-to-end encryption.

title: Student Misuse of Grade Information
description: The student may inadvertently or intentionally misuse the grade information by sharing it with unauthorized parties or using it for purposes other than intended academic planning.
assumptions: Assumes the student has access to the information and may not always use it appropriately.

title: Inappropriate Information Sharing
description: Portal may share more information than necessary for parent access, including potentially sensitive student data beyond grades and feedback
assumptions: Assumes parent access is legitimate but data scope may exceed necessary information

title: Insufficient Notice of Data Sharing
description: Portal may not provide adequate notice to parents about what data is being shared, how it will be used, and with whom
assumptions: Assumes notice requirements exist but may not be fully implemented

title: Unintended Data Exposure
description: Portal may inadvertently expose data to unauthorized parties through misconfiguration or security vulnerabilities
assumptions: Assumes security controls exist but may have gaps

title: Data Flow Meta-data Exposure
description: Meta-data about the data flow (timing, frequency, volume) could be used to link or identify parties
assumptions: Assumes data flow is observable by third parties

title: Parent Inference from Student Data
description: Parent may make inferences about child's academic performance, behavior, or other characteristics from the shared data
assumptions: Assumes parent has access to the data and may analyze it

title: Unintended Data Sharing by Parent
description: Parent may inadvertently or intentionally share the data with unauthorized third parties
assumptions: Assumes parent has access to the data and may share it

title: Inaccurate or Incomplete Information
description: Administrator may input incorrect, outdated, or incomplete information about parent-child relationships, names, or emails, leading to inaccurate records in the system.
assumptions: Administrator may not verify information carefully or may make errors during data entry.

title: Data Minimization Violation
description: Administrator may collect and share more personal data than necessary for the intended purpose, such as including unnecessary personal details in parent-child links.
assumptions: Administrator may not be aware of data minimization requirements or may include extraneous information.

title: Unintended Disclosure of Sensitive Information
description: Administrator may inadvertently disclose sensitive information such as student names, contact details, or relationship information to unauthorized parties during account creation or modification.
assumptions: Administrator may lack proper training or may be careless with sensitive data handling.

title: Data Flow Metadata Exposure
description: Meta-data about the parties involved in the data flow (e.g., who is creating accounts, which parent-child relationships are being established) may be exposed during transmission.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be properly encrypted or may leak metadata through network analysis.

title: Data Integrity Compromise
description: The Grades Portal Web App may not adequately validate or protect the integrity of the parent-child relationship data, allowing unauthorized modifications or data corruption.
assumptions: System may lack proper access controls or validation mechanisms for data integrity.

title: Unintended Data Disclosure
description: The system may inadvertently disclose sensitive parent-child relationship information to unauthorized users or through improper data access controls.
assumptions: System may have insufficient access controls or may leak data through improper logging or reporting mechanisms.

title: Inaccurate Account Records
description: The grading service may write inaccurate or incomplete account records to the account directory, leading to incorrect account information being stored.
assumptions: Assumes the grading service has access to account data that may contain errors or omissions.

title: Unauthorized Data Sharing
description: The grading service may share account records with parent-child relationship links without proper authorization, potentially exposing sensitive account information.
assumptions: Assumes the grading service may not have appropriate access controls or may share data beyond authorized recipients.

title: Data Integrity Compromise
description: The account directory may not properly validate or protect the integrity of account records and parent-child relationship links upon receipt, potentially allowing unauthorized modifications.
assumptions: Assumes the account directory may have insufficient validation mechanisms or access controls.

title: Data Storage Confidentiality
description: The account directory may store account records and parent-child relationship links in a way that exposes sensitive information to unauthorized access.
assumptions: Assumes the account directory may have insufficient encryption or access controls for stored data.

title: Data in Transit Exposure
description: Account records and parent-child relationship links may be exposed during transmission between the grading service and account directory, potentially through interception or metadata leakage.
assumptions: Assumes data may be transmitted over networks that could be vulnerable to interception.

title: Data interception during transit
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transmitted in transit to the cloud hosting provider. If the transmission is not properly encrypted, an attacker could intercept and access this sensitive educational data.
assumptions: Assumes the data flow uses standard network transmission without guaranteed encryption

title: Metadata leakage during data flow
description: The data flow itself may contain metadata about the parties involved (e.g., timestamps, data volume, frequency of transfers) that could be used to link or identify the institution and its operations.
assumptions: Assumes metadata analysis is possible from network traffic

title: Unauthorized disclosure by cloud provider
description: The cloud hosting provider may have unauthorized access to the full grade records, assignments, and account directory, potentially sharing this data with third parties or using it for purposes beyond the original backup/replication purpose.
assumptions: Assumes the cloud provider has appropriate access controls and privacy policies

title: Data storage without adequate security
description: The cloud hosting provider may store the replicated data without adequate security measures, increasing the risk of unauthorized access or data breaches.
assumptions: Assumes the cloud provider's security practices are not fully verified

title: Excessive data sharing at source
description: The Assignment & Grading Service may be sharing more data than necessary for the backup/replication purpose, including full grade records and account directory information that could be sensitive.
assumptions: Assumes the data sharing policy at the source is not optimized for minimum necessary data

title: Data sharing without proper encryption
description: The source element may not be implementing proper encryption before transmitting data to the cloud hosting provider, increasing the risk of interception.
assumptions: Assumes the source has control over encryption implementation
